get.description:
Get all procurements accessible to the authenticated client. Global OAuth keys require organizationId parameter.

**What the list contains.** Real procurements only. Templates, version-procurements (the internal revisions behind a change notice) and imported framework agreements are excluded, so a competition appears once.

**Versions.** Both versions take the same parameters, apply the same access scoping and select the same procurements; they differ only in the field names of the response.

- **v3** (this description) returns external field names: camelCase throughout, including inside the `aboutProcurer`, `procurers` and `directAwardSupplier` values, where `national_id` is exposed as `orgNumber` to match the rest of the external API. `cpvCodes` is `{ mainCPV, additionalCPV }`.
- **v2** returns the raw procurement record, so field names are the snake_case database column names (`total_value`, `framework_agreement_involved`, `about_procurer.postal_address`, …) and `cpv_codes` keeps its stored shape, including the historical `aditional_cpv` spelling. Unchanged, and still the default.

**Choosing a version.** Request `/external/v3/procurements`, or send an `x-api-version: 3` header. A request that specifies neither is served v2, so existing integrations are unaffected.

Only one of the two can be shown here: the API versions by header rather than by path, which OpenAPI cannot express as two separate entries for the same URL.

**Team (`includeTeam=true`).** Returns the users assigned a role on the record itself, each flagged with whether they also hold a role somewhere in the owning organization's tenant tree:
```json
"team": [
  { "email": "anna@oslo.kommune.no", "name": "Anna Hansen", "isActive": true,
    "role": "admin", "isOrgMember": true },
  { "email": "ekstern@konsulent.no", "name": "Ekstern Konsulent", "isActive": true,
    "role": "editor", "isOrgMember": false }
]
```
The whole team is returned, not only the external members — filter on `isOrgMember` to get those. Requesting it on the *list* endpoint is what lets you see, in one call, that the same external consultant has been added to many procurements.

`isOrgMember` is true when the user holds a role in **any** organization in the same tenant tree, not only the one that owns the record. A member of a sibling department is internal to the customer, so a narrower rule would report colleagues as external.

`role` is the role held on this record (`viewer`, `editor`, `admin`) and is a different set from the organization roles returned by `GET /external/{organization_id}/members` — join on `email` if you need to compare the two. `isActive` is false for a deactivated user who is still on the team.**Internal reporting (`includeInternalReporting=true`).** Returns the internrapportering answers already joined to their template questions, so no client has to walk the response document and join on `nodeId` itself:
```json
"internalReporting": [
  { "nodeId": "1651f436-…", "prompt": "Avtaleeier", "type": "input",
    "value": "Vann- og avløpsetaten", "valueText": "Vann- og avløpsetaten" },
  { "nodeId": "9c2ab710-…", "prompt": "Kategori", "type": "checkbox",
    "value": ["Drift", "Vedlikehold"], "valueText": "Drift, Vedlikehold" }
]
```
`value` keeps the natural JSON type (array for multi-choice, number for an amount); `valueText` is the same answer rendered for a spreadsheet cell.

Two rules keep the field set stable, which is what makes the output usable as report rows:

- **Answers to questions that are no longer on the live template are dropped.** A record answered under an older template version can hold responses to questions that no longer exist, and those must not surface as phantom columns. This parameter is therefore *not* an audit trail — `includeCustomFields=true` still returns the complete raw response document.
- **Template questions with no answer are still present**, with `value: null`, so every record in the response yields the same fields.

When the request spans several organizations (`includeSubOrgs=true`) or records built from different templates, the field set is the union of those templates, again so every record has the same fields.

For whole-table reporting, prefer `GET /external/v3/organization/{organization_id}/templates/{template_id}/responses`: it returns every answer to one template as declared `columns` plus flat `rows`, which a spreadsheet or Power BI query can consume without any transformation.

get.description:
Every answer given to one smart-doc template, as a rectangular table ready for a spreadsheet or a Power BI query.

`columns` declares the field set once — `key` is the property each row carries the answer under, `nodeId` is the stable question id, `prompt` is the question text. Each row is then a flat record: identifying fields (`entityType`, `entityId`, `entityName`, `organizationId`, `responseId`, `status`, `createdAt`) plus one property per column. Multi-value answers additionally carry a `<key>_text` twin holding the comma-separated rendering.

```json
{
  "templateId": 412,
  "templateName": "Internrapportering kontrakt",
  "columns": [
    { "key": "n_1651f436ba344106", "nodeId": "1651f436-…", "prompt": "Avtaleeier", "type": "input" },
    { "key": "n_9c2ab710f0ad4c22", "nodeId": "9c2ab710-…", "prompt": "Kategori", "type": "checkbox" }
  ],
  "page": 1, "pageSize": 100, "totalCount": 2, "totalPages": 1,
  "rows": [
    { "entityType": "contract", "entityId": 292, "entityName": "Rammeavtale kontormøbler",
      "organizationId": "oslo-vav", "responseId": 347, "status": "DRAFT",
      "n_1651f436ba344106": "Vann- og avløpsetaten",
      "n_9c2ab710f0ad4c22": ["Drift"], "n_9c2ab710f0ad4c22_text": "Drift" }
  ]
}
```

The columns come from the template's **published** version. Answers to questions that version no longer has are dropped, and questions nobody answered are still present with `null`, so every row has the same shape. A template with no published version returns empty `columns` and `rows` rather than an error.

`createdAt` is when the record first got its response document, not when it was last answered — responses carry no modification timestamp, so this cannot be used to fetch only what changed.

Rows cover every kind of record that can answer a template — contracts, procurements, contract deviations, procurement requests and supplier follow-ups — so filter with `entityType` if you only want one. Procurements answer the internal-request question set of the procurement template they were created from, so ask for that template to get their rows.

On a follow-up row `organizationId` is the **supplier** organization that answered the form, not the buyer asking: a follow-up is answered by the supplier, and the row is yours because the follow-up is on your contract. `entityName` is the form name, `entityId` the follow-up id. Follow-up rows appear only once the follow-up has been answered — its status is REPLIED or EVALUATED — so suppliers' unsubmitted draft answers never show up here. Note that the row's `status` field is the response document's internal status and stays DRAFT on follow-up rows; use the follow-up status, not `status`, to distinguish answered from unanswered.
